airport: broad paved aviation area with runway-like surfaces and sparse surrounding structures, distinguishing airport from railwaystation by lacking concentrated rail lines and station-node organization.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary, distinguishing beach from pond by broader coastal extent and from river by lacking a narrow winding channel.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from viaduct by a more localized crossing form without the strongly elongated elevated-traffic pattern.
commercial: organized urban built-up area with dense man-made structures and road access, distinguishing commercial from parking by stronger building dominance, from residential by larger and more regular building blocks, and from industrial by weaker factory-compound structure.
desert: dry barren land with sparse vegetation and homogeneous exposed-ground texture, visually distinct from other classes by its broad arid surface and lack of strong water, vegetation, or built structure.
farmland: regular cultivated land with visible plot boundaries and agricultural texture, distinguishing farmland from meadow by stronger man-made parcel organization.
footballfield: rectangular sports field with clear field-like geometry and managed grass surface, distinguishing footballfield from meadow by stronger sports-ground structure.
forest: dense natural tree canopy with dark-green continuous vegetation texture, distinguishing forest from mountain by weaker terrain relief and more canopy-dominant appearance.
industrial: factory-like compounds with utilitarian structures, storage areas, and production-oriented layout, distinguishing industrial from parking by stronger building-yard structure, from commercial by more production-oriented compounds, and from railwaystation by weaker rail-line concentration.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture, distinguishing meadow from farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries, from footballfield by lacking formal sports-field geometry, and from river by lacking continuous water structure.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with clear relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from forest by stronger terrain variation.
park: planned green open space with vegetation and leisure-oriented layout, distinguishing park from pond by being land-dominant rather than water-dominant, from commercial by stronger vegetation presence, and from river by lacking a continuous winding channel.
parking: open paved area with vehicle-oriented organization and parking-row structure, distinguishing parking from viaduct by lacking elevated crossing form, from industrial by weaker factory-compound structure, and from commercial by weaker building dominance.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact shape and visible boundary, distinguishing pond from park by being water-dominant, from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline, and from river by lacking a long winding channel.
port: waterfront transport area with dock-side infrastructure and shore-adjacent logistics organization, distinguishing port from river by stronger harbor-side man-made structure and from commercial by clearer shoreline transport context.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railwaystation from viaduct by stronger station-node and rail-line concentration, from industrial by clearer transport-line organization, and from airport by lacking broad aviation pavement and runway context.
residential: built-up neighborhood with repeated housing roofs and regular living-area layout, distinguishing residential from commercial by smaller more repetitive roof structures, from river by lacking water-channel geometry, and from industrial by weaker factory-like yard organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with a continuous winding channel, distinguishing river from pond by stronger linear flow shape, from meadow by clear water dominance, and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with clear grade-separated linear form, distinguishing viaduct from parking by lacking flat vehicle rows, from bridge by a more extended raised-traffic pattern, and from railwaystation by lacking concentrated station-like rail organization.
